numerical_failure.observed_behavior: DatetimeArray.isin / TimedeltaArray.isin can silently truncate finer-resolution values when resolving mismatched time units (because it previously called values.as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True), causing false matches.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: DatetimeArray.isin / TimedeltaArray.isin should avoid lossy downcasting when resolutions differ; it should cast both arrays up to the finer resolution (via _ensure_matching_resos) so that values that differ at sub-unit precision do not match.
trigger_conditions: self and `values` have mismatched resolutions (e.g., 'ns' vs 's', 'us' vs 'ms')
the `isin` operation compares arrays where the `values` contain sub-unit differences that would be truncated when converting `values` down to `self.unit`
prior behavior specifically involved converting with `values.as_unit(self.unit)` using `round_ok=True`

input_output_examples.input: (parametrized test intent) test_isin_mismatched_reso with self_unit,val_unit in [("s","ns"),("ms","us"),("us","ns"),("ns","s")] for dtype_kind in ["M","m"]

oracle_clues: The discrepancy is judged by whether values that differ at nanosecond precision silently match after converting `ns -> s`; the expected result is that they do NOT match (example: [True] -> [False]).
The fix replaces the lossy downcast (`values.as_unit(self.unit)` with `round_ok=True`) with `_ensure_matching_resos`, which casts both arrays up to the finer resolution (no information loss).

category_specific_evidence: Repro example (dtype/precision as units, not numeric dtype): dta = pd.array(pd.to_datetime(["2020-01-01"]).as_unit("s")); vals = pd.array(pd.to_datetime(["2020-01-01 00:00:00.000000001"]).as_unit("ns")); dta.isin(vals) -> Before: [True] (wrong — silently rounded ns value to match); After: [False] (correct — values differ at nanosecond precision).

PR description: DatetimeLikeArrayMixin.isin called values.as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True (the default), which silently truncated finer-resolution values when converting down (e.g. ns -> s), causing values that differed at sub-unit precision to incorrectly match. Fix replaces the lossy downcast with _ensure_matching_resos, which casts both arrays up to the finer resolution (no information loss).

Test added: @pytest.mark.parametrize("self_unit,val_unit", [("s","ns"),("ms","us"),("us","ns"),("ns","s")]) and @pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype_kind", ["M","m"]) in test_isin_mismatched_reso (covering both DatetimeArray and TimedeltaArray).

Test expectation: because 1 in self_unit != 1 in val_unit (unless they happen to be the same unit, which parametrization avoids), isin should be [False, False] (expected = np.array([False, False]); tm.assert_numpy_array_equal(result, expected)).
Test comment: 'isin should not silently truncate finer-resolution values when converting to self's resolution, which leads to false matches.'
Bug note: 'Bug in DatetimeArray.isin and TimedeltaArray.isin where mismatched resolutions could silently truncate finer-resolution values, leading to false matches' (:issue 64545).
reproduction_risks: Evidence is explicitly tied to mismatched time resolutions (e.g. converting ns -> s via values.as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True); reproductions that do not exercise mismatched-resolution conversion may not show the false match.

The parametrized test avoids cases where 1 in self_unit == 1 in val_unit (unless units happen to be the same); reproductions that include such cases may not reproduce the expected [False, False] separation.

provenance.value: DatetimeArray.isin / TimedeltaArray.isin can silently truncate finer-resolution values when resolving mismatched time units (because it previously called values.as_unit(self.unit) with round_ok=True), causing false matches.

DatetimeArray.isin / TimedeltaArray.isin should avoid lossy downcasting when resolutions differ; it should cast both arrays up to the finer resolution (via _ensure_matching_resos) so that values that differ at sub-unit precision do not match.
